mitigation_descriptions: Setting the timestamp_timeout to 0 will require the user to input their password every time sudo is executed. Similarly, ensuring that the tty_tickets setting is enabled will prevent this leakage across tty sessions.

The sudoers file should be strictly edited such that passwords are always required and that users can’t spawn risky processes as users with higher privilege. By requiring a password, even if an adversary can get terminal access, they must know the password to run anything in the sudoers file.
reasoning: The alert sequence confirms unauthorized root privilege execution via sudo by user phopkins on intranet-server (T1548.003). Immediate containment and remediation of the sudoers configuration are necessary to prevent further abuse of elevated privileges.
remediation_plan:
1. Temporarily isolate intranet-server (10.35.35.206) to prevent lateral movement while investigating active processes.
2. Terminate any active unauthorized sudo or elevated sessions associated with account phopkins.
3. Modify the sudoers configuration to set timestamp_timeout to 0 to require password verification on every sudo execution.
4. Enable tty_tickets in the sudoers file to ensure sudo authorization tokens do not persist across multiple TTY sessions.
5. Audit and restrict the sudoers file so that passwords are strictly required and prevent accounts from spawning risky high-privilege binaries.
